I have been farming this land since I was in my twenties. My husband's back has gotten worse, so most of the work falls to me now. We have about 4.5 mu of contracted land plus a small kitchen plot. I know wheat and corn. I know how they look when they are thirsty, when they have bugs, when the soil is right. I will not change what I know works.

Every year I plant winter wheat in October and summer corn on the same land right after the wheat harvest in June. This is what every family here does. The grain station comes and buys it. That is our income. If I tried something new and it failed, we would have nothing to fall back on.

For wheat I go to the seed shop in town and buy the improved seed they have — the same variety I used last two years, it did well. I put down compound fertilizer before planting and urea again when the stalks are coming up. I irrigate four times — once before planting, once in winter to protect from frost cracking, once at jointing, once at heading. The well pump is getting old but it still works. I spray herbicide in early spring when I can see the weeds starting, then I spray for aphids and rust before heading. Three spray rounds total for wheat.

For corn I use the hybrid seeds — the yield is much better than the old types. I plant directly into the wheat stubble without plowing, saves my back. I push on nitrogen because corn is hungry. I only irrigate twice for corn since July and August usually get good rain here.

I keep 0.5 mu separate for garlic — planted in October, harvested in May. I sell some at the village market, eat the rest. My mother's seeds, kept every year. I dig it with a hoe, no machine needed.
